start.text: Wenna's clamp: a low dome of earth and turf gone silver, a stride and a half across, sunk to half the height a clamp should stand. The vents are cold and open. Two of the ring of stakes are down in the moss.
Where the front fell in, the charcoal shows black inside: stick on stick, the shape of the stack still in it, every piece burned clean through and not one gone to ash.
It burned the whole way down with nobody to shut a vent, and never once broke out. A whole burn, a collier's best work, done in the dark while she walked round it.
Wenna's been breaking it out a sack at a time. The best burn she ever had, she says, and she wasn't there for it.
